Goals for this homework:

## Load Libraries 
```{r}
library(tidyverse) 
library(here)
library(patchwork)
library(praise)
library(kableExtra)
```

## Load Data 
```{r}
UlvaFieldData <- read_csv(here("Week_08","Data","Base de datos_cphr.csv"),
                          locale = locale(encoding = "Latin1")) |> # Ask Mica about this 
  mutate(DateTime = mdy_hm(paste(Date, Time))) |>  #Ask Mica about this 
  filter(Site_ID == "Collado" |
         Site_ID == "Atravesado" |
         Site_ID == "San Cristobal" |
         Site_ID == "El Palo" |
         Site_ID == "Laurel") |>  # This dataset had other reef sites that I will be not be using, so I filted the ones I need 
  filter(DateTime >= as.Date("2025-01-01") & 
       DateTime < as.Date("2026-01-01"))
```

This dataset contains monthly seawater water quality measurements collected from coral reef sites in La Parguera, Puerto Rico, between January and December 2025. 

FYI - This dataset was created by my colleague, **Catherine Hernandez**, and will be a part of my final project in this course. I just wanted to go ahead and start on it, and practice writing functions using this dataset to become more prepared for the analysis I'll use for my final project.  

## Writing Functions - Plot 
```{r}
WaterQualityPlot<- function(data = UlvaFieldData, x, y) {
  pal <- c("Atravesado" = "#9E0142", "El Palo" = "#C51B7D", "Laurel" = "#DE77AE", "San Cristobal" = "#F1B6DA", "Collado" = "#4d9221")

ggplot(UlvaFieldData, aes(x = {{x}}, y = {{y}},color = Site_ID, group= Site_ID)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual("Site", values = pal) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 14)
}
```

Here I create a function that will let me plot different water quality parameters over time without having to rewrite the same code over and over. 

## Test - Plot Writing Functions 
```{r}
TempPlot <- WaterQualityPlot(x = Date, y = Temperature_Field) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Temperature (°C)") +
   theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), # This removes the x axis legend title and the values 
    axis.title.x = element_blank()) 

SalPlot <- WaterQualityPlot(x = Date, y = Salinity) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Salinity (PSU)")

TempPlot
SalPlot
```

I tested the functions on temperature and salinity, and it worked! Woohoo! 

## Final Patchwork - Temp and Salinity 
```{r}
#| label: fig-chem-time-series
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

ChemTimeSeries <- TempPlot / SalPlot +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') + # Add the letters to each plot 
  plot_layout(guides ='collect') & # Have one legend 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") # Move legend to bottom

ChemTimeSeries

ggsave(here("Week_08", "Outputs", "Week8HomeworkPlot.png"),
       width = 12,
       height = 8)

praise() # SO beautiful <3
```

@fig-chem-time-series I used patchwork() to combine temperature and salinity into a time series plot. I plan to use this code for my final project and add several other water quality parameters (DO, pH, Nutrients, nDIC, nTA). 

## Writing Functions - Create Summary Stats for each site and each parameter 
```{r}
# https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/programming.html

WaterQualityStats <- function(UlvaFieldData, variable) {
  
  UlvaFieldData |> 
    group_by(Site_ID) |> 
    summarise(min = min({{variable}}, na.rm = TRUE),
              max = max({{variable}}, na.rm = TRUE),
              mean = mean({{variable}}, na.rm = TRUE))

}
```


## Testing Function 
```{r}
TempStats <- WaterQualityStats(UlvaFieldData,variable = Temperature_Field)
SalStats <- WaterQualityStats(UlvaFieldData,variable = Salinity)

TempStats 
SalStats
```

## Creating a Table 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-water-quality-stats

ChemSummary <- TempStats |> 
  left_join(SalStats, by = "Site_ID") |> 
  kbl() |>
  kable_classic() 

ChemSummary
```
